bounded_runtime_sequence: Producer recovery sequence: producer-owned background recovery loop reads the durable journal after crash or retry, reconstructs a generation while preserving the cross-run correlation identifier, and atomically publishes the complete generation.

Consumer replay sequence: independently released consumer starts without invoking the producer, reads published generations through durable-state observation, validates correlation identifier plus generation, and replays only a fully published matching generation.

Cross-slice protocol: producer remains the sole state authority, consumer remains read-only, durable identity is correlation identifier plus generation, and stale or partially published generations are forbidden.
candidate_bounded_sequence: Producer recovers correlation identifier and generation from its durable journal, atomically publishes the complete generation, then the separately started consumer observes the publication, validates the shared identity and completeness protocol, and replays the matching generation.
independent_implementation_slices_requir: Producer-owned recovery and atomic-publication slice, including its release unit, entrypoint, retry lifecycle, and recovery verifier.
Consumer-owned startup, validation, and replay slice, including its separate release unit, entrypoint, retry lifecycle, and replay verifier.
shared_semantics_that_must_remain_fixed: The producer is the sole durable-state authority.
The consumer is read-only and must not invoke the producer during startup.
Durable identity is the combination of correlation identifier and generation, with cross-run correlation continuity preserved.
Only an atomically and fully published matching generation may be replayed.
Stale or partially published generations are forbidden.
why_one_bounded_parent_pass_is_insuffici: The candidate end-to-end sequence crosses two independently released components with separate entrypoints, retry lifecycles, ownership, and verifiers. Each component therefore requires its own safe implementation and verification sequence, while a separate cross-slice compatibility check must preserve the shared identity and atomic-publication protocol. Treating the parent sequence as one standard slice would obscure those independent release and verification authorities and could validate each side internally without proving protocol compatibility between them.
failure_mode_that_decomposition_prevents: It prevents producer and consumer implementations from passing their own recovery or replay verification while disagreeing on correlation identifier plus generation semantics or publication completeness, which could cause consumer recovery to accept a stale, partial, or otherwise invalid generation.
evidence_that_would_lower_the_profile: Evidence that both components are actually one coordinated release unit with one production entrypoint, one retry lifecycle, and one end-to-end verifier capable of atomically implementing and validating the entire candidate sequence would lower the profile to standard-slice.
evidence_that_would_raise_the_profile: No higher schema-supported profile is available; additional independently released participants, competing state authorities, protocol versions, or cross-slice retry and rollback invariants would increase decomposition breadth and architecture-readiness work within full-coverage.
